skill.name: when-auditing-code-style-use-style-audit
skill.description: Audit JavaScript and TypeScript style, compare standards, apply safe auto-fixes, and validate compliance with reports.
skill.summary: Guides code style audits with lint, formatting, standards comparison, auto-fix, and compliance validation.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Reviewed all 216 static findings against SKILL.md, README.md, and PROCESS.md. The detections are false positives from Markdown fences, command examples, local linting scripts, and expected project file operations. No prompt injection, credential access, exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Auto-fix commands can modify source files.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation or dry-run mode before write operations and file renames.

remediation.issue: Tooling commands use npx and project binaries.
remediation.suggestion: Pin versions and prefer package scripts so users know which packages execute.

remediation.issue: Backup examples rely on shell pipelines.
remediation.suggestion: Use null-safe git file lists or document limitations for unusual filenames.

static_findings.snippet: - `quotes`: Project uses double, Airbnb recommends single

content.value_statement: Style drift makes code reviews slower and less consistent. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through scans, reports, safe fixes, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Runs ESLint, Prettier, and TypeScript checks described in the workflow.
Compares project rules against documented standards and common defaults.
Groups violations by priority, rule, file, and fix type.
Applies ESLint and Prettier auto-fixes with backup guidance.
Validates results with linting, tests, build checks, and compliance thresholds.
limitations: Best suited to JavaScript and TypeScript projects with npm tooling.
Auto-fix steps can modify files and require review before commit.
Naming changes need reliable reference checks before renaming files.
Compliance scores depend on project configuration and may need tuning.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Before Review
use_cases.description: Run a dry style scan before opening a pull request and fix formatting issues early.

use_cases.title: Create Team Standards Report
use_cases.description: Compare lint, formatting, and TypeScript settings against documented standards for planning work.

use_cases.title: Add Style Gate to CI
use_cases.description: Use the compliance threshold and report outputs to build a repeatable style check.

prompt_templates.title: Scan Without Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use style-audit to scan this repository for ESLint, Prettier, TypeScript, naming, and organization issues. Report findings only.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Project Standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Use style-audit to compare this project with its documented coding standards. List missing rules, conflicts, and clear recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Reviewed Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use style-audit to create a backup, apply only safe ESLint and Prettier fixes, then show remaining manual work.

prompt_templates.title: Build CI Compliance Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use style-audit to design a CI style gate with a compliance threshold, required reports, and failure criteria.

output_examples.input: Audit a TypeScript service before a pull request.
output: Summary: 91 percent style compliance after formatting fixes.
Most issues were indentation, unused imports, and missing strict TypeScript settings.
Remaining work needs manual review for console statements and type errors.
Prettier and ESLint fixes were applied to supported files.
Tests and build should run before commit because files changed.
CI should publish the style report and fail when compliance drops.
Manual exceptions should be tracked with clear owners.

best_practices: Start with a dry scan before enabling auto-fix.
Review generated changes before committing the result.
Pin tool versions in the project for repeatable results.
anti_patterns: Running auto-fix without a backup or version control state.
Treating sample compliance numbers as project truth.
Renaming files before checking imports and references.

faq.question: Does this skill change files?
faq.answer: It can, when auto-fix steps are requested. Use dry runs and review diffs before commit.

faq.question: Which projects fit best?
faq.answer: It fits JavaScript and TypeScript projects that use npm, ESLint, Prettier, and TypeScript.

faq.question: Can it enforce custom standards?
faq.answer: Yes. It reads documented project standards and compares them with lint and formatting configuration.

faq.question: Does it replace code review?
faq.answer: No. It reduces style noise, but reviewers still need to assess design and behavior.

faq.question: Can it run in CI?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow includes compliance checks, report artifacts, and threshold-based failure criteria.

faq.question: Is auto-fix always safe?
faq.answer: No. Formatting fixes are usually safer than naming changes. Review diffs and run tests after changes.
